promise: The government will halve nitrogen emissions by 2030
description: Rutte's fourth coalition agreement pledged to halve nitrogen emissions in the Netherlands by 2030 to resolve the country's long-running nitrogen crisis, prompting an ambitious livestock reduction plan. The program sparked farmer protests and was later softened, and with the 2030 deadline still ahead the 50% reduction looks unlikely to be met at the current pace.
evidence: Target of 50% nitrogen reduction by 2030 written into the December 2021 coalition agreement
Implementation scaled back after 2023 election losses; 2030 goal at risk per government advisory body (PBL) estimates

review.note: Official archive confirms coalition agreement presented December 15, 2021. Current government page describes later 2035 targets, not proof of the original 2030 formulation. Need archived agreement and PBL forecast for exact pollutant/baseline and assessment.

promise: Pichai said Google aimed to run its operations on carbon-free energy everywhere, at all times, by 2030.
description: Google targets carbon-free electricity for its operations by 2030. Its 2025 report says 2024 total emissions increased 11% while hourly carbon-free-energy use rose from 64% to 66%. Those metrics describe different scopes.
evidence: Pichai's September 14, 2020 post supports the 24/7 operational-energy goal.
Google's 2025 report says 2024 total emissions rose 11% while hourly carbon-free energy reached 66%.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the 2030 target remains future and these are progress indicators with different scopes.

promise: Microsoft will be carbon negative by 2030
description: Microsoft announced its carbon-negative-by-2030 goal on January 16, 2020, alongside a longer-term historical-emissions goal. Its 2024 report says FY2023 Scope 1-3 emissions were 29.1% above the 2020 baseline. The 2030 deadline remains future.
evidence: Microsoft's January 16, 2020 announcement supports the carbon-negative goal.
Its 2024 report gives FY2023 emissions 29.1% above the 2020 baseline.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the 2030 target remains future; the report is progress evidence.

promise: Apple will be 100 percent carbon neutral for its supply chain and products by 2030
description: Apple announced on July 21, 2020 a plan for carbon neutrality across its business, manufacturing supply chain and product life cycle by 2030. Its plan combined a 75% emissions reduction with carbon removal for the remainder.
evidence: Apple's July 21, 2020 release supports the lifecycle goal and its reduction/removal approach.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the 2030 target remains future; the announcement is not proof of completion.

person: Sultan Al Jaber and Simon Stiell
role: COP28 President and UNFCCC Executive Secretary
promise: They called for tripling global renewable-energy capacity and doubling the rate of energy-efficiency improvement by 2030.
description: Their joint call set global 2030 objectives. COP28's stocktake subsequently called on parties to contribute to these objectives; adopting the text did not itself achieve them.
evidence: The July 27 joint statement supports the targets and date.
The December 13 COP28 summary supports their inclusion in the outcome.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the target year remains future and negotiating adoption is not measured delivery.
sources: UNFCCC Stiell and Al Jaber joint statement

promise: BP will reduce oil and gas production by 40% by 2030 versus 2019.
description: BP's August 2020 strategy targeted a 40% reduction in oil and gas production by 2030. Its February 2025 strategy reset instead emphasized increasing oil and gas production and investment.
evidence: BP's 2020 strategy set the 40% reduction goal.
BP's February 2025 reset shifted investment and planned production toward oil and gas.

review.note: The 40% production target belongs to the August 2020 strategy, not the February net-zero announcement. The 2023 step was a weakening to 25%, not an immediate growth pledge; the 2025 reset increased planned production. This is a withdrawn-target judgment, not a measured 2030 outcome.

promise: Increase annual low carbon investment tenfold to around $5 billion a year by 2030.
description: BP's August 2020 strategy targeted roughly $5 billion of annual low-carbon investment by 2030. In February 2025 BP reset transition-business investment to $1.5-2 billion annually, more than $5 billion below its intervening guidance.
evidence: BP's August 2020 strategy set a tenfold increase in low-carbon investment.
The February 2025 reset reduced planned transition investment while increasing oil and gas investment.

review.note: Announcement date is August 2020. The $5bn reduction in 2025 is relative to intervening guidance, not subtraction from the original $5bn target. Original exact wording is a paraphrase. The assertion about 2023-24 spending and dropping all EV charging targets was not supported.

person: World Health Organization (cervical cancer elimination strategy)
promise: Meet 90-70-90 cervical cancer elimination targets by 2030
description: WHO's cervical-cancer elimination strategy was adopted in August 2020 and launched in November. Its 2030 goals cover 90% HPV vaccination of girls by age 15, 70% screening of women by age 35 and again by 45, and 90% treatment or management of cervical disease.
evidence: The official strategy sets 2030 vaccination, screening and treatment targets; full achievement remains prospective.

promise: Reduce global methane emissions by at least 30% from 2020 levels by 2030
description: Launched by the United States and the European Union at COP26 in Glasgow in November 2021, the Global Methane Pledge commits signatories to cut global methane emissions by at least 30% from 2020 levels by 2030. The pledge has catalysed new policies and the IEA's Global Methane Tracker 2026 found that regulations in place would cut oil and gas emissions by only around 20% by 2030 — well short of the 30% economy-wide target, with agriculture lagging furthest.
evidence: The pledge launched in 2021 with more than 100 countries; by the 2026 IEA report membership exceeded 150.
Its collective 2030 target is at least 30% below 2020 anthropogenic methane emissions across sectors.

review.note: More than 100 countries joined at launch; more than 150 is a later membership count. This is a collective global anthropogenic-emissions aim, not a uniform national 30% obligation. The 20% oil/gas policy projection and exact launch day need additional supporting lines; retain pending for the future 2030 objective.

person: Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use signatories
promise: Halt and reverse forest loss and land degradation by 2030
description: The 2023 Forest Declaration Assessment found 6.6 million hectares of global gross deforestation in 2022, 21% above the pathway to end deforestation by 2030. Tropical primary forest loss was a separate 4.1 million hectares, 33% above its required pathway.
evidence: The assessment reports separate all-forest deforestation and tropical-primary-forest loss measures.

review.note: Record conflates 2022 global gross deforestation (6.6m ha, 21% off path) with tropical primary forest loss (4.1m ha, 33% off path). These findings were in the 2023 assessment, not a 2025 assessment. Exact original signatory count/launch wording still needs the declaration.

promise: Double Europe's share of global semiconductor production to 20% by 2030
description: The EU Chips Act, in force since September 2023, set the goal of raising Europe's share of global semiconductor production to 20% by 2030, backed by over 43 billion euros in public and private investment. Commission projections and independent analyses as of 2025-2026 put Europe's share on course to stagnate at roughly 10-12% by 2030, well short of the target, though the act has catalysed new fabs and investment.
evidence: Europe's share projected at ~11.7% by 2030, versus the 20% target
Europe currently holds around 10% of the global semiconductor market
EU Chips Act entered into force 21 September 2023

review.note: Audit supports the 20% goal and 11.7% 2030 projection, explicitly a forecast not an outcome. September 2023 entry into force is not the original announcement of the Digital Decade target. Exact 21 September date and EUR43bn composition not verified here; retain pending.

promise: Call for an SDG Stimulus of at least $500 billion a year for developing countries
description: The Secretary-General launched the SDG Stimulus proposal on February 17, 2023, after advocating it earlier that month. The proposal seeks additional development financing and requires action by governments and international financial institutions.
evidence: Guterres called for the $500bn-a-year stimulus in February 2023
A Leaders Group was announced to implement the initiative
No mechanism delivering the annual $500bn level existed as of 2026

review.note: Public launch was February 17, not February 16; he had already called for G20 action on February 13. This is a financing proposal directed to governments and institutions, not a personal guarantee to disburse $500 billion. No precise 2030 delivery deadline or exhaustive 2026 outcome assessment established.

promise: Finance and facilitate $1 trillion in sustainable finance by 2030, including $500 billion in environmental finance and $500 billion in social finance
description: Citi announced the goal on April 15, 2021, expanding its earlier $250 billion environmental-finance commitment. The target counts financing and facilitation from 2020 through 2030, with environmental and broader social categories.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the source establishes the 2020-2030 financing-and-facilitation target, but the original cumulative total was not reconciled to the latest report's tables.

promise: Achieve carbon neutrality across Tencent's own operations and supply chain by no later than 2030, with 100% green power by 2030
description: Tencent announced its operations-and-supply-chain carbon-neutrality target on February 24, 2022, together with 100% green electricity by 2030. Its mid-term report says green electricity rose from 22.0% in 2024 to 48.5% in 2025; the 2030 outcome is not yet due.
evidence: Tencent reports 48.5% green electricity in 2025, against its 100% target for 2030.

promise: Tesla will sell 20 million vehicles per year by 2030
description: Tesla omitted its goal of delivering 20 million vehicles annually by 2030 from the impact report released in May 2024. Removal from a report is evidence of changed emphasis, not on its own proof of a formal cancellation or the eventual 2030 result.
evidence: Tesla omitted the 20-million target from its 2023 impact report
TechCrunch (July 2026): Musk 'abandoned that idea a few years ago'; Tesla made its 10 millionth EV

review.note: Omission in May 2024 supports removal from that report, not by itself a formal withdrawal or failure before 2030. Exact Battery Day formulation and July 2026 ten-millionth-unit assertion were not established.

promise: Provide up to €150 billion in defence-industry loans to member states through the SAFE instrument
description: The Council adopted SAFE on May 27, 2025, allowing up to EUR150 billion in loans on demand against approved national plans through 2030. By April 2026 it had authorized funding for 18 member states.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: Council approvals do not establish the amounts actually disbursed; the financing window remains open.

role: UN General Assembly High-Level Meeting on HIV/AIDS
promise: Political Declaration on HIV/AIDS: 'United to End AIDS by 2030' - end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030
description: A large majority of UN member states adopted the June 23, 2026 political declaration reaffirming the goal of ending AIDS as a public-health threat by 2030. Adoption is not achievement of the health target.
evidence: WHO's June 24 report identifies the previous day's adoption and the 2030 goal.

promise: Mobilize funding for Gavi's 2026-2030 strategy to immunize 500 million children and avert an estimated 8-9 million future deaths
description: Gavi launched its investment opportunity on June 20, 2024. The June 25, 2025 summit secured more than $9 billion in pledges toward an $11.9 billion strategy budget. Pledges are not cash receipts, and modeled future deaths averted are not completed outcomes.
evidence: Funding pledges advanced the programme, but 2026-2030 immunization delivery and modeled benefits remain prospective.

promise: "Looking beyond Helios, we plan to launch a new rack-scale AI platform every year"
description: On August 4, 2026, Su described plans for a new rack-scale AI platform annually after Helios. The call places the initial Helios ramp near the end of Q3 2026, with a larger Q4 ramp, not before Q3.
evidence: Lisa Su's statement on AMD's Q2 2026 earnings call, August 4, 2026
Helios rack-scale system on pace to ship before Q3 2026

review.note: Annual cadence statement supported. Source's 'before Q3' conflicts with earnings transcript's end-Q3 initial ramp; August already lies in Q3. No2030 endpoint to cadence commitment established.

promise: Plan, as conditions stood in April 2021, to make Cadillac an EV-only brand by 2030
description: Cadillac's April 21, 2021 statement presented an EV-only 2030 plan with an explicit current-conditions qualification. July 2026 reporting confirmed renewed gasoline-model plans.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: renewed gasoline models weaken the trajectory, but the retrieved evidence does not establish the final 2030 sales mix or a definitive cancellation of that specific deadline.
sources: Car and Driver: gasoline model plans

promise: Make the entire Rolls-Royce Motor Cars product portfolio fully electric by 2030
description: Rolls-Royce announced full portfolio electrification by 2030 on September 29, 2021. In March 2026, CEO Chris Brownridge publicly abandoned the target.
evidence: The target was expressly withdrawn, rather than merely remaining incomplete before its deadline.

promise: Turn Nigeria into a $1 trillion economy by 2030
description: Finance minister Doris Uzoka-Anite discussed the government's USD 1 trillion ambition and the sustained growth required in a February 25, 2026 ministry report.
evidence: Finance minister reiterated the $1 trillion economy agenda in February 2026
Administration ties the 2030 goal to the 2026 National Development Plan

review.note: February 25 source attributes the statement to minister Doris Uzoka-Anite under Tinubu's agenda and calls for 10%-12% growth over the next decade. It does not substantiate Tinubu personally promising USD 1 trillion by 2030.

promise: Invest $165 billion in the United States to build three new fabs, two advanced packaging plants and an R&D center in Arizona
description: TSMC announced plans to expand its US investment from USD 65 billion to USD 165 billion, including three additional fabs, two advanced packaging facilities and an R&D centre.
evidence: The March 2025 TSMC announcement describes planned investment, not money already spent or completion of all facilities.

review.note: The additional USD 100 billion was part of the March 2025 announcement bringing the total to USD 165 billion; do not double-count it as a second increase without separate evidence. No 2030 completion deadline for the entire package was established; distinguish Taiwan release date from US appearance.

role: South Korean shipbuilder and engine maker
promise: Invest KRW 1.0722 trillion in engine and SMR-component facilities, supporting a target of 7.2 GW annual HiMSEN capacity by 2030
description: The September 10, 2026 disclosure allocates KRW 833.6 billion to the engine facility and KRW 238.6 billion to SMR components. It targets engine-plant completion in May 2028, SMR completion in first-half 2029 and total engine capacity of 7.2 GW by 2030.
evidence: The company release states separate facility schedules and a 2030 combined marine and land-based engine-capacity target.

promise: Invest more than $2 billion in Latin American programming and sports rights between 2027 and 2030
description: Prime Video said it would spend more than $2 billion on original and licensed programming and live sports rights across Latin America between 2027 and 2030, more than doubling its local original output across Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia and Chile and releasing more than 25 new titles in 2027 alone.
evidence: Announcement of August 20, 2026
Commitment covers 2027-2030 across five Latin American markets

promise: Establish at least one functional national emergency medical team in each WHO African Region member state by 2030
description: The regional committee adopted an emergency-medical-team framework during its August 2026 session. The framework targets nationally owned, deployable teams by 2030.
evidence: WHO reports adoption and progress in individual countries, not universal completion; exact adoption day remains unresolved.

review.note: The commitment covers WHO African Region member states, not every AU country. The September 7 story reports August adoption; the provisional agenda places discussion August 27 but is not proof of the final vote date. September 9 is unsupported and cannot simply be replaced with a publication date.

role: Indian subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Group
promise: Reach 20 percent women in its executive workforce by 2030
description: Hyundai Motor India announced a target on September 7, 2026 for women to represent 20% of its executive workforce by 2030.
evidence: The company announcement supports the date, target, denominator and 2030 horizon.
